question: Compare supervised and unsupervised learning.
answer: Supervised learning uses labeled data to learn a mapping from features to a target, suitable for classification and regression tasks [S1] [S2]. In contrast, unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data, aiming to discover patterns or group similar examples [S1] [S2].

citations.title: Ml Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Supervised and Unsupervised Learning Machine learning builds models that learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. In supervised learning every training example has a label: the model learns a mapping from features X to a target y. Classification predicts a category, such as spam or not spam; regression predicts a continuous number, such as a house price. In unsupervised learning there are no labels and the goal is to discover structure. Clustering, for example k-means, groups similar examples, and dimensionality reduction, for example PCA, compresses features while keeping most of the variance. Semi-supervised learning mixes a small labeled set with a large unlabeled set, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards obtained by acting in an environment.
